# Define the tutorial packaging format

## Description

This epic defines the packaging format that makes curated tutorials versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. The format covers tutorial metadata, pinned images, and a validation manifest, so that a tutorial is a self-contained, versioned artifact that the Dashboard tutorial gallery can list and launch and that automated validation can check.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial packaging format specification:
  - Tutorial metadata (identity, journey coverage, targeting information needed to launch the tutorial into a user's project)
  - Image pinning (how the notebook/workbench image a tutorial runs on is pinned so the tutorial is reproducible)
  - Validation manifest (what is checked to consider a tutorial valid and tested)
- Establish versioning rules so a tutorial can evolve independently of Dashboard releases
- Provide a reference example/template showing how a tutorial is packaged in the format
- The format must serve both notebook-based tutorials (launched by opening a workbench with the notebook) and pipeline-based tutorials (launched by importing the pipeline)

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification is documented and covers tutorial metadata, pinned images, and a validation manifest
- A reference tutorial packaged in the format passes validation driven by its manifest, with its images pinned as specified
- A tutorial packaged in the format can be versioned and re-validated without a Dashboard release
- The format demonstrably supports both a notebook-based tutorial and a pipeline-based tutorial (one reference example of each)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1 — inherited as P0 because this format gates the P0 tutorial gallery and curated tutorial work): tutorial packaging format defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases

## Notes

- Because the format is consumed by pipeline-based as well as notebook-based tutorials, the RHOAI Pipelines team is a stakeholder in and reviewer of the format specification, even though the format is owned by the Notebooks/Workbenches team.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated surface from which a user can launch a tutorial into their own project with one click — opening a workbench with the tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline. The gallery reads tutorial metadata from the tutorial packaging format and surfaces the curated, tested tutorial set.

## Scope

- Add a tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard (navigation entry, listing of available tutorials with their metadata)
- Implement one-click launch mechanics into the user's own project:
  - Notebook tutorials: create/open a workbench in the user's project with the tutorial notebook
  - Pipeline tutorials: import the pipeline into the user's project
- Read tutorial identity, targeting, and pinned-image information from the tutorial packaging format so tutorials are consumed as versioned content independent of Dashboard releases
- Surface enough information per tutorial for a new user to pick a getting-started journey (title, description, journey coverage)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can browse the tutorial gallery from the Dashboard and see the curated tutorials with their metadata
- Launching a notebook tutorial from the gallery creates/opens a workbench in the user's project containing the tutorial notebook, running on the pinned image
- Launching a pipeline tutorial from the gallery imports the pipeline into the user's project
- End-to-end launch is verified against at least one tutorial packaged in the agreed tutorial packaging format
- The gallery renders and launches tutorials that were versioned independently of the current Dashboard release (no Dashboard change required to pick up a re-versioned tutorial)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline)

# Curated notebook tutorials for core getting-started journeys

## Description

This epic authors the five notebook-based curated tutorials covering the core getting-started journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is substantive authored content (a maintained, tested notebook), packaged in the tutorial packaging format so it is versioned and testable, and launchable from the Dashboard tutorial gallery into the user's project.

## Scope

  1. First workbench — creating and using a first workbench
  2. Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench
  3. First training run — training a first model
  4. First deployment — deploying a first model
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation application
- Package each tutorial in the agreed tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)
- Keep each tutorial maintained: tested against the current release, with updates when the platform or pinned images change

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering the listed journeys, each packaged in the agreed tutorial packaging format
- Each tutorial passes the validation defined by its manifest
- Each tutorial has been run end-to-end successfully against the current release
- Each tutorial launches into a workbench in a user project via the Dashboard tutorial gallery one-click launch

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for the tutorial gallery: how to use the gallery and launch tutorials, and the contribution process for adding new tutorials. It is substantive documentation content delivered through the Red Hat docs content process, written after the implementation work so it describes what was built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Using the tutorial gallery
  - Finding and browsing tutorials in the Dashboard
  - Launching a notebook tutorial into a workbench in your project
  - Launching a pipeline tutorial by importing the pipeline
- Contributing new tutorials
  - The tutorial packaging format and what a tutorial artifact must contain (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)
  - How a tutorial is versioned, validated, and tested against the current release
  - The process for proposing and landing a new curated tutorial (documented process only — no submission tooling this release)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the tutorial gallery: browsing, and launching both notebook and pipeline tutorials
- Published documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials, including the packaging format requirements

- The documentation does not describe any tutorial submission tooling (out of scope this release)
